notes:
VERDICT: PASS. Neither of the two preprod defects reproduces on production -- production confirms the index's CORRECTED declarations are right, and preprod's original raw behavior (before correction) was the true platform behavior all along, not a preprod-only artifact.

=== DEFECT 1 SIDE BY SIDE: result_status ===
Preprod (original, pre-correction diagnosis): v2 returned ONLY {field_value}, missing id/internal_name/field_name/colour that the schema then required together -- scored DRIFT, then the index was corrected to declare field_value alone with guidance saying the others are 'deliberately dropped here and never appear'.
Prod (this probe): identical -- {field_value} alone, on 3/3 independently sampled real results (Failed, Passed, Blocked), across 2 different runs and 2 different case folders. id/internal_name/field_name/colour absent on every row.
CONCLUSION: prod agrees with the CORRECTED declaration. The correction was right; preprod was not the odd one out and neither is prod. Both preprod and prod cut result_status down to field_value -- this is genuine, consistent v2 serializer behavior, not an environment quirk. (v1's sibling list_test_results_for_test_case_by_integer_id, re-checked here on the SAME 3 underlying result rows via TR-4827350/TR-3866741, still returns the full result_status object with id/internal_name/field_name/colour/value_category on prod -- so the v1-vs-v2 serializer split observed on preprod also reproduces exactly on prod.)

=== DEFECT 2 SIDE BY SIDE: custom_fields ===
Preprod (original): declared type object, returned []  -- scored DRIFT, then v2's index entry was corrected to declare an array (v1's was left as object, uncorrected).
Prod (this probe): custom_fields:[] on 3/3 real results -- an array, matching the corrected v2 declaration exactly.
CONCLUSION: prod confirms the v2 correction was right. (Not in scope for this v2-only retest, but noted for completeness: v1's own schema for custom_fields is still declared object and returns [] on the same prod result rows -- carrying the SAME uncorrected mismatch preprod's v1 sibling finding flagged; that finding's proposed fix -- correct v1 the same way v2 was corrected -- still applies and still hasn't been done.)

=== configuration_id CROSS-CHECK (v1 sibling) ===
Task asked to check configuration_id on the v1 sibling, where preprod found the declared key entirely ABSENT (not null) on all rows. Re-checked here on prod: TC-5508207 and TC-1041809's v1 results (list_test_results_for_test_case_by_integer_id, hyphenated test-results key) both come back with NO configuration_id key at all in the JSON -- same declared_missing pattern as preprod, reproduced exactly, including that v2's own configuration_id (this capability under test) DOES appear as an explicit null on the same underlying rows. The v1-vs-v2 asymmetry on this field is confirmed real and environment-independent, not a preprod fluke.

=== PROD DATA THAT REMAINS UNPOPULATED (an honest miss, not a fabricated find) ===
The task asked to specifically hunt for populated attachments, step_result/test_run_step_result, dataset and configuration_id, since preprod never had any. Real effort was spent looking: 3 closed runs with genuinely logged results were found and read (TR-4827350 x2 cases, TR-3866741 x1 case), a 4th case with real Jira issue links was found and checked (TC-681528, but it turned out never actually executed -- issues sit on the case, not a result), and a 21-case and 28-case run were also scanned for configuration matrices or dataset-driven mappings. None were found: every real result in this project fixture is a plain case-level manual submission with no configuration, no dataset, no step-level breakdown, and no attachments (attachments:[] on the v1 sibling, which is the only one of the two capabilities that declares the field at all -- v2 doesn't return or declare attachments). So these four fields remain UNVERIFIED IN THEIR POPULATED FORM even after using real production data -- 'PASS' above is scoped strictly to the two defects actually asked about (result_status, custom_fields) and the configuration_id cross-check, not a claim that the whole schema is now fully exercised.
